1. Whether Reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

2. To be referred to the Reporter or not?

 

Justice J.D. Kapoor, President (Oral)  

1. Admittedly respondent purchased a PC from the appellant for a cost of Rs. 32,000/-. On the allegation that within three months of the purchase the PC stopped working as there was a major break down. However, respondent-1 also insured the PC with the United Insurance Company(Respondent-3). When he lodged the claim with the insurance company, the same was rejected on the basis of the report of the surveyor that the components listed in the bills were actually not installed in the PC in dispute. Consequently, the respondent filed the instant complaint against the appellant seeking refund of the cost of the PC which was highly defective.

 

2. Vide impugned order dated 29.11.2003, the complaint was allowed by the District Forum with direction to the appellant either to replace the defective PC with new one with fresh warranty or to refund Rs. 32,000/- with interest @9% p.a. and Rs. 5,000/- towards compensation for mental agony and harassment caused to the respondent and Rs. 2,000/- as cost of litigation.

 

3. Through this appeal the impugned order has been assailed mainly on the ground that respondent-1 had a remedy against the insurance company with whom the PC was insured and not against the appellant. We do not subscribe to this view for the simple reason that the complaint was filed by the respondent-1 for refund of the cost of goods like PC which was found defective. Section 3 of the consumer Protection Act provides the consumer an additional and independent remedy for seeking compensation or refund of the cost and many other things on the allegations of deficiency in service or for having been sold a defective article or unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practice. Merely because the respondent-1 had also insured the PC with the respondent it did not mean that he did not have any remedy against the manufacturer or the seller of the PC if the PC is found to be defective.

4. Quality and standard of any goods are to be tested on the anvil of definition of word defect as defined by section 2(1)(f) of the Act. Defect means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or (under any contract, express or implied or} as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any good.

 

5. In terms of Section 14 of the Consumer Protection Act whenever the goods sold by the trader are found to be defective and in this case the defects in the PC were demonstrated from the report of the surveyor coupled with it having been broken down within 3 months, the Consumer Forums has the discretion to order the service provider or the trader to do one or more of the following things :-

(a) to remove the defect pointed out by the appropriate laboratory from the goods in question;
(b) to replace the goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect;
(c) to return to the complainant the price, or, as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant;
(d)              to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation to the consumer for any loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party[Provided that the District Forum shall have the power to grant punitive damages in such circumstances as it deems fit;]
(e) to [remove the defects in goods] or deficiencies in the services in question;
 

4. We do not find any infirmity in the finding returned by the district Forum so far as the defect is concerned but set aside the interest awarded by the District Forum as ordinarily interest is awarded where there is such a term between the parties or where there are equitable grounds. It is not the case that the respondent-1 had not used the PC. He had used the PC for 3 months. Interest is awarded mainly in the case of deposits against cost of flat or plot or fixed deposit if the benefit of such deposits has not been obtained or received by the consumer.

 

5. In the result, we partly allow the appeal by maintaining the direction to refund the cost of PC as well as the amount of Rs. 5,000/- awarded towards the compensation and set aside rest of the order.

 

6. Payment shall be made within one month from the date of receipt of this order.

       

7. Bank Guarantee/FDR, if any furnished by the appellant, be returned forthwith.

 

8. A copy of this order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to Record room.

9. Copy be sent to Presidents of all the District Forums.

10. Announced on 26th day of November, 2007.

         

(Justice J.D. Kapoor) President       (Rumnita Mittal) Member         ysc
